title: Frobenius functional on a finite-dimensional commutative Hopf algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. A commutative Hopf $k$-algebra here means a unital commutative $k$-algebra $A$ with $k$-algebra maps $\Delta_A:A\to A\otimes_k A$, $\epsilon_A:A\to k$, $S_A:A\to A$ such that $(\Delta_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=(1\otimes\Delta_A)\Delta_A$, $(\epsilon_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=(1\otimes\epsilon_A)\Delta_A=1_A$, and $\mu_A(S_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=\mu_A(1\otimes S_A)\Delta_A=\eta_A\epsilon_A$, under the usual tensor unit and associativity identifications; $\mu_A$ and $\eta_A$ are multiplication and unit. Tensor products are those of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Let $H$ be such a commutative Hopf $k$-algebra admitting a finite $k$-vector-space basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. There exists a $k$-linear functional $\lambda:H\to k$ for which the map $\Phi_\lambda:H\to\operatorname{Hom}_k(H,k)$ given by $\Phi_\lambda(a)(x)=\lambda(xa)$ is bijective. Here $\operatorname{Hom}_k(H,k)$ is the vector space of $k$-linear maps $H\to k$, with pointwise addition and scalar multiplication.

source.place: Siqi Clover Zheng, Frobenius Algebra Structure in Hopf Algebras and Cohomology Ring with Poincare Duality (17 October 2020), Theorem 4.15, printed p.10, and proof of Theorem 4.8, pp.9-10: the product pairing induces a bijection with the linear dual in finite dimension. Read online at https://math.uchicago.edu/~may/REU2020/REUPapers/Zheng,Siqi.pdf; local document WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag asserts this Hopf-algebra theorem.

proof.text: Choose $0\ne\lambda\in C$ and $x_0\in H$ with $\lambda(x_0)\ne0$. Define $t:C\to k$ by $t(f)=f(x_0)/\lambda(x_0)$. Then $t(\lambda)=1$, so $j:H\to H\otimes_k C$, $j(h)=h\otimes\lambda$, has left inverse $h\otimes f\mapsto t(f)h$, well-defined by the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Thus $T=\mu\circ j$ is injective and $T(h)(x)=\lambda(S(h)x)$.

proof.text: If $S(h)=0$, then $T(h)=0$, hence $h=0$. Since $S$ is $k$-linear, it is injective. Its domain and codomain are the same finite-dimensional space $H$, so [lem-sfb-finite-linear-injective-surjective] makes $S$ surjective.

source.place: Proposition 4.12(2), Theorem 4.13, proof of Theorem 4.14 and Theorem 4.8, printed pp.8-10; agent adaptation using a right coinvariant functional directly. Online source read; local PDF WANTED. Farnsteiner HopfMod2, pp.1-2, confirms the action/coaction conventions.

proof.text: Define the $k$-linear map $\Phi(a)(x)=\lambda(xa)$. If $\Phi(a)=0$, choose $h$ with $S(h)=a$. Commutativity gives $T(h)(x)=\lambda(ax)=\Phi(a)(x)=0$ for every $x$; injectivity of $T$ gives $h=0$ and hence $a=0$. Thus $\Phi$ is injective. By [lem-sfb-linear-dual-dimension-rank], $H^*$ is finite-dimensional with $\dim_kH^*=\dim_kH$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-linear-injective-surjective] to $\Phi:H\to H^*$ to obtain surjectivity and hence the required bijection.
